rationale: B wins because it finds the harder, more useful story hiding in the weak facts: "Verdano's three utility pilots are the story its funding round isn't" names the buyer, the proof burden, and the trade reporter's real question. A is cleaner, but it is too cautious where it matters; "No angle can stand on this until a utility is named and a result exists" throws away the best conditional route instead of shaping it honestly. B needs copy surgery for overclaiming, but it gives a founder sharper strategic choices.
gaps_in_A: "No angle can stand on this until a utility is named and a result exists" is too absolute. A customer-story angle can stand as a conditional trade pitch if it is built around pilots, procurement, and named-proof needs.
"someone who ran systems inside Tesla Energy" invents seniority and responsibility not in the update. The facts only say ex-Tesla Energy.
"Community-solar grids are hitting a load-balancing wall" overstates a category claim before the independent evidence exists.
It misses the skeptical headcount/procurement tension in "plans to hire 10 engineers" against three unnamed pilots and no disclosed revenue.
gaps_in_B: "Ex-Tesla Energy and NREL engineers" invents that the founders are engineers. The update only says they are ex-Tesla Energy and ex-NREL.
"community solar breaks the grid before rooftop does" is an overreach. The update says grid strain, not that community solar breaks the grid or beats rooftop solar to the problem.
"Community solar creates real feeder-level headaches" adds technical specificity not supplied by the update. Plausible is not the same as grounded.
"A 14-person startup is hiring 10 engineers to sell into utility procurement" is a useful tension, but it muddies engineering hiring with sales/procurement strategy; that needs cleaner proof.
